Thus, ships, even though they go with full sails, nonetheless seem to stand still. Someone will eventually demonstrate in which parts <note>of the heavens</note> comets wander, why they travel so far removed from the others, and how great and of what kind they are. Let us be content with what has been discovered; let posterity also contribute something to the truth. One says: "We do not see beyond through the stars, but we transmit our sight through comets." First, if that happens, it does not happen in that part where the star itself consists of thick and solid fire, but where the thin splendor runs out and disperses into hair <note>the comet's tail</note>. You see through the intervals between the fires, not through the fires themselves. One says: "All stars are round, but comets are stretched out, from which it appears they are not stars." For who will grant you that comets are long, when their nature indeed is a globe like the rest? However, the brightness is extended just as the sun sends its rays far and wide. Yet the sun itself has one shape, and the light that flows from it has another. Thus the body of comets itself is rounded, but their splendor appears longer than that of other stars. Why, you ask? Tell me first why the moon receives a light so very different from the sun, since it receives it from the sun? Why is it sometimes red, sometimes pale? Why does it have a livid and black color when it is excluded from the sight of the sun? Tell me why all the stars have a face somewhat unlike each other, and most different from the sun. Just as nothing prevents them from being stars even though they are not similar, so nothing prevents comets from being eternal and of the same lot as the others, even if they do not have a similar face. Furthermore, if you consider the world itself, is it not composed of diverse things? Why is it that the sun always burns in Leo and parches the lands with heat, but in Aquarius it binds the winter and closes the rivers with frost? And yet both this star and that one are of the same condition <margin>† rises</margin>, although they are dissimilar in effect and nature. Aries is passed through <note>original: "excolitur"</note> in a very short time, Libra sinks most slowly, and yet this star and that are of the same nature, though the former ascends in a brief time and the latter is brought forth for a long duration. Do you not see how contrary the elements are to each other? There are heavy and light things, cold and hot, moist and dry. The whole harmony of this world consists of discord. You deny a comet is a star because its shape does not correspond to the pattern, nor is it similar to the others. For you see, that star which returns to its place in the thirtieth year <note>Saturn</note> is very similar to this one which revisits its seat within a year. Nature does not perform its work according to a single pattern, but prides itself in variety. It made some things slower, others swifter than the rest. Some it made stronger, others more temperate; some it led out from the crowd so that they might proceed as individual and conspicuous things, and some it sent into a flock. He is ignorant of nature's power who does not think she is sometimes permitted to do what she does not do frequently. She does not show comets often; she has attributed to them another place, other times, and motions unlike the rest. She wished to honor the magnitude of her work through these, whose face is too beautiful for you to think them accidental, whether you consider their size or their brightness, which is greater and more burning than the others. Indeed, the face has something notable and singular, not cast into a narrow space and compressed, but released more freely and embracing the region of many stars. Aristotle says that comets signify storms and the intemperance of winds and rains. What then? Do you not judge that to be a star which announces future events? For this is not a sign of a storm in the same way that oil sparking and the growth of rotten fungi are signs of future rain, or the way it is an indication of a raging sea if the coots play on dry land and desert their familiar marshes and the heron flies above the high cloud. But it is so in the way that the equinox is a sign of the year turning toward heat or cold; or the way those things which the <term>Chaldaeans</term> <gloss>astrologers</gloss> chant, regarding what a star ordains as sad or joyful for those being born. That you may know this is so, a comet having risen does not immediately threaten winds and rains, as Aristotle says, but <margin>The rising of a comet makes the whole year suspicious.</margin> it makes the whole year suspicious. From which it appears that it did not draw signs from the immediate vicinity to give to the immediate vicinity, but has them stored up and compressed by the laws of the world. That comet which appeared in the consulship of Patruculus and Vopiscus brought about what was predicted by Aristotle and Theophrastus. For there were great and continuous storms everywhere. Indeed, in Achaia and Macedonia, cities were overthrown by earthquakes. Slowness, he says, is an argument that they are heavier and have much of the earthly in them. Moreover, their very courses are generally driven toward the poles <note>original: "cardines"</note>. Both are false. I will speak of the former first: that those things which are carried more slowly are heavy. What then? Is the star of Saturn, which completes its journey most slowly of all, heavy? <summary>Seneca defends the celestial nature of comets by comparing their diversity to other planetary phenomena and the general discordia concors of the universe. He refutes Aristotle's view of comets as mere weather signs, arguing they follow divine laws and long-term cycles.</summary>
